claims.hypothesis: Can the surface density be measured from optically thick CO emission using emitting heights?
claims.experiment: Semi-analytical model inverting emitting heights and temperatures to CO column and surface density, applied to 14 disks
claims.result: Surface density profiles and masses obtained for all 14 disks with large (dex-level) uncertainties
claims.finding: The method works on optically thick emission at the cost of larger uncertainty, dominated by the emitting-height error

evidence.quote: In this work we provide a method to measure the disk surface density from optically *thick*, rather than *thin* as commonly done, emission.

claims.hypothesis: Is a vertically isothermal model adequate when only one line is available?
claims.experiment: Compare isothermal masses (brightness temperature at emitting height) with stratified masses across the sample
claims.result: Average ratio 0.8 with ~0.2 dex spread; midplane temperature overestimates by ~6
claims.finding: Isothermal model with brightness temperature at the emitting surface is a satisfactory approximation

evidence.quote: We conclude that, when only one line is available, using the isothermal model and using the brightness temperature at the emitting surface to set the temperature is a satisfactory approximation.

claims.hypothesis: Do 12CO and 13CO give consistent surface densities with a standard isotopic ratio?
claims.experiment: Compare 12CO and 13CO masses and fit a linear relation
claims.result: Slope 1.1 +/- 0.2, 13CO mass higher on average, normalization 2.5 +/- 0.8 dex, compatible within uncertainties
claims.finding: Good general agreement; any isotopic ratio deviation cannot be confirmed given the large errors

evidence.quote: We note however that this value has a large error, meaning that the two mass estimates remain compatible within the uncertainties.

claims.hypothesis: Is CO depleted in these disks relative to the ISM abundance?
claims.experiment: Compare CO-derived masses (x_CO = 1e-4) with dynamical masses from rotation curves
claims.result: CO-derived masses are systematically lower; median depletion about 20 and average about 50
claims.finding: CO is depleted in protoplanetary disks

evidence.quote: implying that CO is depleted by a median factor $\sim$20 with respect to the ISM value, in line with other works that find that CO is depleted in proto-planetary disks

claims.hypothesis: Does the simple direct model reproduce full thermochemical emitting heights?
claims.experiment: Compare direct-model emitting heights with DALI models for several disk masses and stellar types, fitting N_ph
claims.result: Good match for N_ph of about 3-6e16 cm^-2, with 13CO using the isotope-rescaled N_ph
claims.finding: The simple model captures the main physics and can be calibrated with a single N_ph

referee_caveats_inferred: The 25 per cent emitting-height error is borrowed from a benchmark, so all quoted errors (dex-level) are not statistical; depletion factors inherit this
Depletion factor depends on dynamical masses that themselves assume self-similar profiles
N_ph calibrated against a single DALI grid with fiducial parameters; dependence on grain growth and UV not explored
Isotope normalization of 2.5 dex versus text 'factor 2.5' is stated inconsistently
Sample is those disks where heights are measurable, so biased toward large, bright, intermediate-inclination disks
